Batch B-38213 was originally scheduled to be issued at 02:00 UTC, but due to a 3-hour time zone deviation in cross-regional collaboration, it was actually executed ahead of schedule at 23:44 local time. Within 11 minutes of issuance, 24 stations across 3 cities successively reported "community shutdowns" and "S1 interface anomalies," involving a total of 61 base stations and 9 dedicated line users. The rollback script was executed at 08:51, and by 12:51, all alerts were cleared, restoring normal business. Verification confirmed that 7 parameter templates were modified in this batch, 2 of which conflicted with the neighbor zone switching threshold and did not perform grayscale verification according to the process before issuance.
Additionally: The weak signal issue reported by an administrative duty staff member at a certain hospital was verified to be a fault in the hospital's self-built laboratory, and a follow-up TK-20261114-8353 was established.
This impact has constituted a regional-level event, and the duty engineer has been called according to the procedure and reported to the duty manager.

Body: Starting {date}, the 100G port of one {device} at {site} reported 4–6 times per day for 3 consecutive days that the optical module receive power was below the lower limit; the threshold is -14dBm, and measured values were -19.2 to -20.5dBm; after replacing the pigtail and cleaning the flange, it was still out of limit. The same-model port of another {device} at the same site has normal receive power of -9.8dBm; the OTDR curve for this cable section is flat with no breakpoints, and there have been no change orders at this site in the past 30 days, so configuration factors can be ruled out.
According to current criteria: if the same port is still out of limit after replacing connectors, other ports on the same cable are normal, and there is no breakpoint and no change, it is judged as optical module hardware degradation, classified as hardware failure, not as optical cable interruption and not as configuration change.
Call conditions: hardware-type alarms that remain unrecovered for ≥24 consecutive hours trigger a duty call; this time it has lasted 72 hours, and this port carries 3 government and enterprise dedicated lines, so the condition is met; it is recommended to send personnel at night with {batch} spare parts to replace the optical module.
Impact classification: only one site {site}, no other sites affected, counted as single site.
(The cutover window for {customer}'s {order_no} has been moved to next week and is unrelated to this review.)

Impact grading: only the {device} board is affected, with 1 cell within a single station affected; cumulative impact score = 1×1=1, classified as single-site.

Caller: {customer} reported being unable to access the internet near {site}; call duration 3 minutes 20 seconds.

[Approval note · {ticket}]
Submitted by: network operations duty technician; approved by: duty supervisor; {date} {time}

Reason: At the four base stations {site}, {site}, {site}, and {site}, since {time}, 4G user-plane downlink PRB utilization has remained at 92%~98%, 5 cells in the same batch reported congestion discard alarms, and the discard count increased by 1.2 ten-thousand packets within 30 minutes; the capacity expansion board request must first be graded and then queued.

Verification conclusion: None of the four stations is out of service, mains power and batteries are normal, there are no cable section alarms, there are no configuration change records in the past 30 minutes, the board has not reset, and the optical module receive power of -9dBm is normal, so it does not belong to the four categories of cable cut, power supply, configuration, or hardware; the characteristics are a sudden traffic surge with PRB and discard count rising simultaneously.

Determination criteria: Root cause classification—multiple stations on the same cable section simultaneously losing optical signal is a fiber cut, mains interruption or battery undervoltage is a power interruption, a configuration change in the past 30 minutes with no similar alarm before the change is a configuration error, repeated resets of boards or optical modules with hardware alarms is a hardware fault, and sudden traffic with rising congestion discard counts is congestion; if none apply, there is no persistent fault. Call scoring—congestion alarms lasting more than 30 minutes score 40 points, involving 3 or more sites scores 40 points, user-plane discard rate above 1% in the same batch of cells scores 20 points, totaling 100 points, reaching the 80-point threshold, so the duty engineer must be called immediately to intervene with rate limiting and capacity expansion. Impact grading—4 affected sites falls in the 2 to 4 range as multi-site, 1 is single-site, 5 or more is regional-level, and only a single board single port is local partial.

Attachment: Spare parts for {order_no} have arrived at the {site} warehouse and are unrelated to the grading of this order.

Upon verification, the busy-hour headroom of the 3 neighboring cells is 8%, 11%, and 9% respectively, all insufficient to accept offload. Also attached: {device} had one transmission bit error alert yesterday, which has been handled by the transmission team and is unrelated to this ticket. Overall determination: capacity expansion needs to be arranged, the action is to expand the existing link or cell, and the utilization tier is tier 4. Please reply with the schedule before {date}.

state: Internal email: From Radio Optimization Engineer, To Duty Dispatch Team, Cc Network Optimization Team Leader. Subject: Handling opinion on {case_id} ({date}). All, since {time} yesterday, the {device} attached to {site} has shown S1 interface signaling congestion on the 5G side, accompanied by cell-level PRB utilization of 96%; interference and transmission factors have been ruled out. This matter can be fully resolved through remote network management operations: first, adjust the neighbor cell handover threshold; second, raise the load sharing parameter from 30% to 55%; third, remotely restart the baseband board; all three are within the authority of the network operations center and require no personnel to visit the site. The specific criteria are as follows: if all handling actions fall within the scope of network management parameter adjustment / remote restart / remote switching, it is determined as remotely resolvable; if any one of board replacement, fiber replacement, tower work, or entering the equipment room for plugging/unplugging occurs, it is determined as requiring on-site attendance. Ownership is divided by the primary specialty of the handling actions: parameter adjustment and remote restart belong to the network operations center, access-segment outside plant belongs to field operations and maintenance, optical channels belong to the transmission specialty, routing and backbone belong to the core network specialty, and CPE and customer equipment rooms belong to customer-side installation and maintenance. The handling actions in this ticket are all parameter changes and remote restarts, so it belongs to the network operations center. SLA score criteria: the three sub-items are summed, with impact scope 4, service 3, risk 3, full 10 points; 0-3 routine, 4-5 standard, 6-7 urgent, 8 or more critical. In this ticket, impact scope 3 points (affecting 2 residential communities), service 3 points (there are already 11 user complaints and some users cannot access the Internet), risk 3 points (continued congestion will cause cell out-of-service), totaling 9 points. After the fault, a hard reset was performed site by site on all affected sites; 25 cells recovered within 10 minutes after reset, and traffic returned to 95% or more of baseline; the remaining 2 cells were due to an abnormal port on the same {device} board and the board was replaced overnight. No similar alarms recurred after the reset. Looking back over the past 7 days, the same batch of equipment had 3 brief interruptions, all accompanied by short-term jumps in port CRC counts that then automatically cleared. Per the review criteria: if the fault can be eliminated by a hard reset, there are 2 or more records of the same type of brief interruption in the past 7 days, and no optical power over-limit or power supply abnormality is found, it is classified as a board or optical module hardware fault; if it cannot be eliminated after reset, or there are no repeated records in the past 7 days, it is classified as no persistent fault. On-call criteria: if a single hardware fault can be resolved by part replacement and the single-site outage is less than 60 minutes, it is set to the temporarily no-call tier. Impact tier mapping: 9 sites are involved but all are within this area, so it is tiered as multi-site level. Additional note: the complaint follow-up call for {customer} has been completed by the customer service team.

state: Shift handover note: on {date} {time}, a fault was received for {customer}'s 100G wavelength channel {ticket}. The transmission engineer's preliminary review found an abnormal cross-connection configuration on the OTN wavelength channel network management side; the service is still carried by the backup channel and there is no obvious customer-side perception. The judgment criteria follow the shift consensus: if the fault point is within the network management operable range and no on-site replacement of pigtails or boards is required, it is always regarded as remotely recoverable; if it involves access-segment outside plant, customer-premises CPE, or board replacement, an on-site visit is always required. Team ownership is divided by specialty: optical transmission and wavelength channel maintenance belong to the transmission specialty, routing and backbone equipment belong to the core network specialty, and network management configuration adjustments and remote handling belong to the network operations center. Our judgment is that this is a remote configuration adjustment, to be handled by the network operations center. Urgency uses cumulative scoring: no service interruption scores 0 points, non-key customer scores 0 points, and the fault has not triggered a customer complaint scores 0 points, for a total of 0 points; 0-1 points is routine, 2-3 points is standard, 4-5 points is urgent, and 6 points or more is critical, so it is classified as routine. This time, 52 communities have still been recalled, requiring call for duty. Note: The review meeting {date} {time} was moved to Meeting Room 3, unrelated to the decision.
